string.name: online_profile_privacy_note
string.comment: Privacy note on the Online Profile settings screen. Sprites are character images; metadata is their non-image information.

resources.string: Only your character sprites and metadata are shared.

Online Profiles are exclusively opt-in and designed with privacy and security in mind. Enabling one publishes your current trainer and active monster, including their selected sprites, at a shareable link. If you change your team later, your Online Profile updates to match. Servers do not store your phone number, contact list, call history, or other personal or sensitive data. Links between MonsterDialer profiles and contacts stay exclusively on each device.

Anyone you send your sharing link to can find your profile through its randomly generated public ID. Tap “Regenerate sharing link” to invalidate the current public ID and create a new one. The previous link will no longer work for anyone you shared it with.
Tap “Delete Online Profile” to permanently remove your published profile data. Anyone who has your sharing link will no longer be able to view your team through it.

string.name: characters_help_title
string.comment: Title of the in-app guide explaining MonsterDialer characters and character packs.

string.name: characters_help_description
string.comment: Short description below the Character Guide title. The roster system is the set of player and contact battle characters.

string.name: characters_help_intro_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide introducing the player's character collection.

string.name: characters_help_intro_message
string.comment: Introductory Character Guide paragraph. Player Character and Contact Characters are names of settings; translate consistently with their UI labels.

resources.string: The Character tab is your central hub for personalizing every call. You can choose a character to represent you (Player Character) and assign different characters to each of your contacts (Contact Characters).
Your team is the trainer and active monster shown here. They represent you in every battle during a call. Tap either one to choose a different character.

Your roster is the set of up to six monsters you choose for your team. Drag and drop custom monsters to reorder it as you like. The first monster in the roster is your active monster for call battles.

string.name: characters_help_creating_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide about making custom characters.

string.name: characters_help_creating_message
string.comment: Character Guide instruction for creating a trainer or monster. “Add trainer” and “Add monster” refer to UI actions; translate consistently with those labels.

resources.string: Tap “Add trainer” or “Add monster” in the respective settings to create your own. You can pick images from your gallery for:

string.name: characters_help_creating_sprites_front
string.comment: Character Guide bullet explaining front sprites. Preserve the bold Front Sprite label and translate it consistently with the sprite picker label.

resources.string: Front Sprite: Seen by you when this contact calls.

string.name: characters_help_creating_sprites_back
string.comment: Character Guide bullet explaining back sprites. Preserve the bold Back Sprite label and translate it consistently with the sprite picker label.

resources.string: Back Sprite: Seen as your own character during battles.
Give your character a name and add its sprite artwork. The front sprite is used when the character appears as an opponent, while the back sprite represents the character on your team during battles.

Choose an image file available through your device’s image picker. MonsterDialer does not impose a fixed resolution or file-size limit for custom sprites. For the clearest result, use PNG artwork with a transparent background, keep the character centered with minimal empty padding, and use a similar scale and pose for front and back sprites.

For monsters only, open Advanced and turn on the Radiant switch to add a radiant variant. Character selection will then show regular and radiant versions of the same monster. The radiant version starts locked and must be found during battles before it can be selected. A front sprite is required because the Find feature uses it to discover and unlock the radiant variant.

string.name: characters_help_advanced_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide about optional monster settings.

string.name: characters_help_advanced_message
string.comment: Character Guide explanation of monster settings. Advanced, Level, Max HP, and Radiant refer to UI labels; translate consistently with those labels.

resources.string: For Monsters, you can expand the “Advanced” section to set their Level and Max HP. You can also toggle the “Radiant” status manually for characters you create yourself.

string.name: characters_help_sharing_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide about sharing and importing characters. Preserve the ampersand or use the locale's equivalent.

string.name: characters_help_sharing_message
string.comment: Character Guide introduction to the two shareable MonsterDialer file types. Keep the trailing colon or use equivalent punctuation.

resources.string: MonsterDialer uses two types of shareable files:

string.name: characters_help_sharing_files_character
string.comment: Character Guide bullet describing a .monstercharacter file. Preserve the bold file extension and do not translate it.

resources.string: .monstercharacter: A single character with its stats and artwork.

string.name: characters_help_sharing_files_pack
string.comment: Character Guide bullet describing a .monsterpack file. Preserve the bold file extension and do not translate it.

resources.string: .monsterpack: A collection of multiple characters, often themed.

string.name: characters_help_sharing_how_to
string.comment: Character Guide instruction for exporting and importing characters. Do not translate the .monstercharacter extension; translate Import character consistently with the button label.

resources.string: Long-press any of your custom characters to export them as .monstercharacter files. To import either type, simply open a file someone sent you or use the “Import character” button.

string.name: characters_help_packs_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide about creating shareable character packs.

string.name: characters_help_packs_message
string.comment: Character Guide instruction for creating a character pack. Character Packs and Create pack refer to UI labels; do not translate the .monsterpack extension.

resources.string: To share a collection of your custom monsters, you can create a Pack. Go to “Character Packs” and tap “Create pack” (this button appears once you’ve created at least one character). Select the monsters you want to include, and you can then export the final .monsterpack file to share with others. A pack can contain up to 200 characters and its compressed size must not exceed 24 MiB.

Tap “Import pack” to add a .monsterpack file someone shared with you. Imported characters become available to select when the pack is enabled. Only import artwork and sounds you created or are licensed to use.

string.name: characters_help_radiants_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide about discovering rare radiant monster variants.

string.name: characters_help_radiants_message
string.comment: Character Guide explanation of radiant monsters. Radiant is the app's term for a rare sparkling variant; “in the wild” means a non-contact battle during a call.

resources.string: Radiant monsters are rare, sparkling variants. Unlike normal characters, variants in packs are locked until you encounter them “in the wild” during a call. Once found, they unlock automatically for your collection, and you can share a special discovery card to show off your find!

string.name: characters_help_management_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide about managing characters in the player's roster.

string.name: characters_help_management_message
string.comment: Character Guide instruction for managing custom characters. Your monsters, Your trainers, Edit, Share, and Delete refer to UI labels; translate them consistently.

resources.string: Long-press any character in the “Your monsters” or “Your trainers” sections to Edit, Share, or Delete it. Built-in characters and those from imported packs cannot be modified.

Characters are grouped by source: Built-in characters come with the app; Your trainers and Your monsters are characters you created in the app; and imported characters are organized by their character pack. Long-press a character you created to edit, share, or delete it.

Characters are grouped by source: Randomize is available for contacts only and automatically chooses an eligible character for each call; Built-in characters come with the app; Your trainers and Your monsters are characters you created in the app; and imported characters are organized by their character pack. Long-press a character you created to edit, share, or delete it.

string.name: characters_help_assignments_title
string.comment: Section heading in the Character Guide about assigning characters for calls.

string.name: characters_help_assignments_message
string.comment: Character Guide introduction to the two character-assignment modes. Keep the trailing colon or use equivalent punctuation.

resources.string: There are two ways to use characters:

string.name: characters_help_assignments_player
string.comment: Character Guide bullet explaining Player Character. Preserve the bold label and translate it consistently with the settings title.

resources.string: Player Character: This is your avatar. Set it in “Player Character” settings to represent you in every call.

string.name: characters_help_assignments_contact
string.comment: Character Guide bullet explaining Contact Characters. Preserve the bold label and translate it consistently with the settings title.

resources.string: Contact Characters: Assign specific monsters or trainers to individual contacts in “Contact Characters.” They will appear as your opponent when they call you.
